info.description: REST API of the Wattson server, which controls a Merach exercise bike. Authenticate with an API token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or the session cookie set by the login flow. A state-changing request authenticated by the session cookie (this includes routes that document no scope, such as logout) is refused with 403 `csrf` when its Origin header names a foreign host or, with no Origin, the browser reports `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. Bearer-token requests are exempt.
info.title: Wattson API

get.description: Returns every configured OIDC provider ordered by display name, enabled or not. Client secrets are never returned. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Adds a provider such as Authentik, Keycloak or any other OpenID Connect server. The slug becomes part of the login and callback URLs and cannot be changed. Register the returned `redirect_uri` at the provider. A duplicate slug returns 409 `slug_taken`. The client secret is sealed at rest and never returned. Requires the `admin` scope.

Fetches the discovery document at the URL (the `.well-known/openid-configuration` suffix is added when missing), timing out after 5 seconds, and reports the issuer it publishes. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. Requires the `admin` scope.

delete.description: Removes the provider. Users who signed in through it keep their accounts and sessions, but can no longer sign in with it. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Returns one provider. The client secret is never returned; `client_secret_set` says whether one is stored. Requires the `admin` scope.

patch.description: Changes the fields present in the body. The slug cannot be changed. `client_secret` replaces the stored secret when present; an empty string is rejected with 400, so omit it to keep the current one. A change takes effect on the next sign-in; sessions already open are unaffected. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Verifies a local username and password and sets the session cookie. Attempts are rate limited per remote IP address (the connection's address; X-Forwarded-For counts only when the connection comes from a proxy listed in `auth.trusted_proxies`, and then the rightmost address that is not a trusted proxy is used): after 10 failures in 10 minutes every attempt from that address, whatever the username, returns 429 `rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Unknown user, wrong password, disabled user and password-less (OIDC) users all return the same 401 `invalid_credentials`. Returns 403 `local_login_disabled` when password sign-in is turned off and the user is not the bootstrap admin. No authentication required.
Deletes the current session, if any, and clears the session cookie. No authentication required.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user, the scopes of the credential in use, and whether it is a session or a token. Requires the `read` scope.

The redirect URI registered at the provider. Checks the provider's `error` parameter, the signed state cookie (same provider, same `state`), exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier, verifies the ID token and its nonce, applies the allowed groups and emails, finds, links or creates the local user, syncs admin status from the admin group, and starts a session. Always answers 302: to the `return_to` path on success, otherwise to `/login?error=<code>` where code is one of `unknown_provider`, `provider_unavailable`, `provider_error`, `state`, `exchange_failed`, `forbidden`, `not_provisioned` or `inactive`. No authentication required.

parameters.description: State echoed by the provider; must match the state cookie.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Error code from the provider, when it refused the sign-in.
parameters.name: error

get.description: Redirects (302) the browser to the provider's authorization endpoint using the authorization code flow with S256 PKCE and a nonce, and sets the short-lived `wattson_oidc` cookie that binds the attempt to this provider. `return_to` must be a same-origin path (it must start with a single `/`); anything else is replaced by `/`. An unknown or disabled provider redirects to `/login?error=unknown_provider`, and one whose discovery fails to `/login?error=provider_unavailable`. No authentication required.

parameters.description: Same-origin path to open after signing in, for example `/settings?tab=bike`. Default `/`.
parameters.name: return_to

post.description: Changes the signed-in user's password. Session only: an API token gets 403 `session_required`. A wrong current password returns 400 `invalid_current_password`. All of the user's sessions are deleted and a fresh session cookie is set. Requires the `read` scope.

get.description: Lists the ways to sign in: whether setup is pending, whether password sign-in is enabled, and the enabled OIDC providers ordered by display name. No authentication required.

Returns the state of the single bike this server controls: idle, connecting, ready, riding, paused or finished, the bound rider, the live protocol and any connection problem with advice to fix it. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Binds one of the caller's riders to the bike (or the simulator) and returns at once with state `connecting`; watch `GET /api/bike` or the WebSocket for `ready` or a connection problem. Any user with control may drive the single bike. Returns 409 `bike_busy` unless the bike is idle, 400 `no_bike_address` when the settings name no bike, and 404 for a rider that is not the caller's. Requires the `control` scope.

Returns the bike to the rider's minimum level and closes the link. Does nothing when idle. Refused with 409 `ride_active` while a ride is riding or paused; use release to end the ride too. Returns 424 `floor_unconfirmed` when the bike was released but not confirmed back at its minimum level. Requires the `control` scope.

Ends any ride, returns the bike to the rider's minimum level and closes the link. Idempotent: releasing an idle bike succeeds. Returns 424 `floor_unconfirmed` when the bike was released but could not be confirmed back at its minimum level; the rider must then lower the resistance at the console. Requires the `control` scope.

Scans for Bluetooth devices for `duration_s` seconds (default 5) and lists them, supported bikes first. Empty transport fields use the saved settings. Refused with 409 `bike_busy` while a bike is connected or another scan runs; 424 `scan_failed` when the adapter or proxy cannot be used. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Returns the latest ride snapshot: state, speed, power, cadence, distance and resistance level. In state `idle` when no bike is connected. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Starts, pauses, resumes or stops the ride, or changes the resistance level. Any user with control may drive the single bike. Returns 409 `no_bike` when no bike is connected and 409 `bad_state` when the command does not fit the ride state (for example resume while not paused). Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns the caller's riders, ordered by ID. A user with no rider gets a default one (named after their display name or username) created on the first call. An admin may pass `all=true` to list every user's riders; other users get 403. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.description: Admin only: list the riders of every user instead of only your own.
parameters.name: all

schema.description: Admin only: list the riders of every user instead of only your own.

post.description: Creates a rider owned by the caller. Omitted fields take their documented defaults. Requires the `control` scope.

delete.description: Deletes one of the caller's riders. The last remaining rider cannot be deleted (409 `last_rider`), nor can the rider bound to the connected bike (409 `rider_in_use`; disconnect the bike first). A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns one of the caller's riders. A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `read` scope.

patch.description: Changes the fields present in the body of one of the caller's riders. The merged profile is validated (`min_level` must not exceed `max_level`). A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Changing the rider bound to the connected bike is allowed, but the connection keeps the profile it was made with: the change applies at the next connect. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns every route, newest first, without geometry. Routes are shared: every signed-in user sees all of them. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Uploads a GPX, TCX or FIT file (multipart/form-data, field `file`, at most 20 MiB) and stores it as a route owned by the caller. Tracks without elevation, or above 60 degrees latitude, are looked up at OpenTopoData when that is enabled in Settings. Errors: 400 `unsupported_format` or `no_track`; 413 `too_large`; 422 `no_elevation` (enable OpenTopoData elevation in Settings → Integrations), `route_too_short` (under 50 m), `route_too_long` (over 500 km) or `too_many_points`; 502 `elevation_unavailable` (the elevation service failed). Requires the `control` scope.

parameters.description: Route name. Defaults to the name stored in the file, else the file name without its extension.
parameters.name: name

schema.description: Route name. Defaults to the name stored in the file, else the file name without its extension.

file.description: The route file: GPX, TCX or FIT, at most 20 MiB. The format is detected from the content, then the file name.

post.description: Creates a route from constant-grade segments ridden in order, for example to train a specific climb. The route starts at 100 m elevation. The total length may not exceed 500 km (422 `route_too_long`). Requires the `control` scope.

delete.description: Deletes a route. Only the route's owner or an admin may do this (403 `not_owner` otherwise). A route the connected ride is using cannot be deleted (409 `route_in_use`); stop the ride first. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns a route with its bounding box, simplified GeoJSON line and spec. Any signed-in user may read any route. Requires the `read` scope.

patch.description: Changes the route's name. Only the route's owner or an admin may do this; anyone else gets 403 `not_owner`. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns the route resampled every `step_m` metres as parallel arrays (latitude, longitude, elevation, grade). The response is gzip-compressed when the client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. Requires the `read` scope.

Returns the whole configuration. Secrets are write-only: each is reported as a `*_set` boolean (`bike.esphome_key_set`, `ha.token_set`, `mqtt.password_set`, `mapillary.token_set`, `strava.client_secret_set`) and the value is never returned. Requires the `admin` scope.

patch.description: Changes the fields present in the body and leaves the rest alone. Secret fields are write-only: omit one to keep the stored value, send an empty string to clear it, or send a value to replace it. The merged result is validated as a whole; a bad value returns 400 `invalid_setting` with the message `<section.field>: <problem>` and nothing is stored. Returns the new settings in the same shape as the GET. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Scans for 5 seconds with the local adapter or the ESPHome proxy and looks for the bike's address. Without an address it only reports how many devices were seen. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. Refused with 409 `bike_busy` while a bike is connected, because one adapter cannot scan while holding a bike. Requires the `admin` scope.
post.summary: Test the Bluetooth adapter and bike

post.description: Connects to the ESPHome device, performs the encrypted handshake and reads its device info, then disconnects, timing out after 5 seconds. It never subscribes to Bluetooth and never talks to the bike, so it is safe during a ride. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. A device without the Bluetooth proxy component reports `no bluetooth_proxy`. Requires the `admin` scope.

Calls `GET {url}/api/` with the token as a bearer credential, timing out after 5 seconds. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. A 401 from Home Assistant reports `token rejected (401)`. Requires the `admin` scope.

Creates the bootstrap admin, optionally saves the public URL, and signs the new admin in with a session cookie. If saving the public URL fails after the admin was created, the failure is logged and the admin is still created. Fails with 409 `already_setup` once any user exists. No authentication required.

schema.description: Session cookie for the new admin.

get.description: Reports whether first-run setup is still needed. No authentication required.
Returns the caller's own API tokens, without their secrets. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Creates a token for the signed-in user and returns its plaintext exactly once. Session only: an API token gets 403 `session_required`. The scopes must be held by the caller, otherwise 403 `scope_exceeds`. Requires the `read` scope.

delete.description: Deletes one of the caller's own tokens. Revocation takes effect immediately. A token owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns every user account, ordered by ID. Requires the `admin` scope.

patch.description: Changes a user's admin or disabled flag. Disabling a user deletes all of that user's sessions. The bootstrap admin cannot be demoted or disabled (409 `bootstrap_protected`), and the last enabled admin cannot be removed (409 `last_admin`). Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Returns 200 while the server is running. No authentication required.

Upgrades to a WebSocket that streams the bike status and ride ticks and accepts ride commands. Offer the `wattson.v1` subprotocol (400 without it); authenticate with the session cookie (the Origin header must name this server or the public URL, else 403) or by also offering the subprotocol `bearer.<token>`. At most 32 connections are open at once, 8 per user (503 beyond that). The message formats are in the AsyncAPI document, docs/asyncapi.yaml. Requires the `read` scope.
